verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'two-hour launch window that opens at 6:24 p.m. ET on Wednesday'; R2: 'Launch: 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 2026'; R3: 'lift off at 6:24 p.m. on April 1'; R4: '6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday'; R6: '04/01/2026 06:24:00 PM EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the date and day as Wednesday, April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission has a two-hour launch window opening at 6:24 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'two-hour launch window that opens at 6:24 p.m. ET'; R2: '6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday... with a two-hour window'; R3: 'between 6:24 p.m. ET and 8:24 p.m. ET'; R4: '6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday'; R6: 'Launch Window... Duration (Mins): 120'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state a two-hour window opening at 6:24 p.m. ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch window is 6:24 p.m. – 8:24 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'anytime after 6:24 p.m. ET and anytime before 8:24 p.m. ET'; R3: 'between 6:24 p.m. ET and 8:24 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for the exact window times in sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch will take place from Launch Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Launch location: Launch Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center near Cape Canaveral, Florida'; R1/R3/R4/R5: consistently 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly specifies Pad 39B at KSC Florida; others confirm location.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '10-day flight', '10-day journey'; R3: '10-day journey'; R4: '10-day journey'; R5: '10-day journey'; R7: 'mission will last approximately 10 days'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state 10-day mission duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'circumnavigating the moon'; R2: 'around the moon and back'; R3: 'which they will orbit but not land on'; R4: 'looping around Earth and the moon'; R5/R7: similar 'around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe mission as orbiting/circumnavigating the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'returning humans to deep space for the first time in five decades'; R3: 'first manned mission toward the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R4: 'first people to launch toward the moon since the Apollo 17 mission in 1972, more than 50 years ago'; R5: 'first time since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 (1972), over 50 years.

verifications.claim: Live coverage of the Artemis II launch starts at 10 a.m. ET on floridatoday.com/space and NASA+ / YouTube.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Full coverage... kicks off at 10 a.m. ET on launch day... at floridatoday.com/space'; also 'NASA+... YouTube'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly matches Florida Today at 10 a.m. ET and mentions NASA+/YouTube.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '80% chance that it will be a go'; R8: '80% chance of favourable weather conditions'

verifications.claim: If the Artemis II launch does not occur on April 1, the next available launch window is available through April 9.

verifications.reasoning: Official schedule shows windows through April 6, not April 9.
